lead.hed: Sailors and Marines man the rails as USS Ashland arrives for San Francisco Fleet Week
lead.insight: A Navy still posted overnight shows sailors and Marines manning the rails aboard the dock landing ship USS Ashland as she arrived for San Francisco Fleet Week. The photograph was taken Oct. 6 and released early Wednesday. The caption says this is the 45th Fleet Week, a public look at the maritime services in the Bay Area. It is a port visit, not a deployment order.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Aaron Sandoval-Mendoza, U.S. Navy · DVIDS 9996500 · Public domain · Sailors and Marines man the rails aboard USS Ashland (LSD 48) on arrival for San Francisco Fleet Week, Oct. 6, 2026.

political.hed: Public Discourse asks whether Germany will lift its ban on surrogacy
political.insight: Wednesday’s essay says a so-called altruistic surrogacy contract can avoid some commercial extremes, including material exploitation and harsh terms. It says the basic problem remains: a child is conceived in the interest of others, and the biological mother is treated as a means to an end. The piece is an argument about a pending German debate, not a vote count.

political.hed: Law & Liberty says Buckley argued for a formative university, not a neutral one
political.insight: Wednesday’s forum essay says William F. Buckley was, in his fashion, an academic-freedom advocate, but he argued for a university that forms students rather than one that claims no view. It is a reading of Buckley’s case, not a campus news item.

political.hed: Heritage says Canada’s assisted-suicide system has claimed more than 100,000 lives
political.insight: Tuesday’s commentary says that since 2016, assisted suicide has claimed more than 100,000 Canadian lives. It cites a 26-year-old with depression who shopped for a doctor to sign off on his death, and a disabled man who applied for medical assistance in dying because he feared going homeless. The piece treats involuntary euthanasia as the next step in that descent.

political.hed: France fires an upgraded nuclear-capable missile from a submarine
political.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that the nuclear-powered ballistic-missile submarine Le Vigilant fired an M51.3 in an acceptance test after the boat’s overhaul. The missile carried no nuclear warhead. It launched off Finistère in western France and splashed down in the North Atlantic. President Macron called the shot a test of France’s strategic credibility.

tech.hed: 53rd Wing testers ran Black Flag with the Navy at Point Mugu
tech.insight: DVIDS reported Tuesday that the 85th and 422nd Test and Evaluation Squadrons tested emerging capabilities with joint and allied partners at Naval Base Ventura County from Sept. 10 to 25. The event ran with the Navy’s Gray Flag exercise so units could share range time. Capt. Kaleb Nypaver, 85th TES director of operations, said the point was a test no one squadron could run at home station.

tech.hed: Pentagon names four directed-energy weapons for a base counter-drone pilot
tech.insight: Defense News reported Tuesday that the Pentagon named four systems for a homeland counter-drone pilot Congress ordered: AeroVironment’s Palletized High-Energy Laser, Epirus’ Leonidas high-powered microwave, Kord’s Firefly high-energy laser, and Boeing’s Compact Laser Weapon System. Joint Interagency Task Force 401 will field them at U.S. bases. Army Brig. Gen. Matt Ross said the year-long pilot is meant to show how to integrate and sustain the weapons, not to declare them ready.

culture.hed: First Things says the case for AI doom is radically uncertain
culture.insight: Wednesday’s essay recalls a week in September when an obscure Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, became briefly famous after resigning. The writer treats the doom talk that followed as a claim that outruns what anyone can actually know. It is an argument about certainty, not a lab finding.
